# Purpose

These sessions teach the **principles of reproducible research** — transparency, provenance, and documentation that outlives the project — together with the everyday **workflows** that put them into practice.

Students organise a project folder and write documentation for **their own PhD project**, then transfer that text into the course assignment's Swedish Research Council DMP template. There is no hand-in to the team that runs these two days.

Success criterion — the **5-year test**: someone returning in five years, the student or a colleague, can understand what was done and which decisions were made. It holds for qualitative, survey, trial, and secondary-data projects alike.

Teaching time is **two afternoons of Team-Based Learning (3 h each)**, each preceded by a guided self-study morning (3 h). Day 1 afternoon is hybrid (room Future + Zoom), Day 2 is Zoom-only, so every team activity must work in breakout rooms.

# Learning outcomes

By the end of the two days, the student can:

1.  **Explain** the principles of reproducible and open research — transparency, provenance, raw versus derived material, FAIR versus open — and use them to justify choices in their own project.
2.  **Structure** a durable project folder and its documentation (README, decision log, naming and versioning) so the project passes the 5-year test.
3.  **Track** changes and decisions in a form that humans and tools can both read, and justify which versioning approach fits their project.
4.  **Draft** Swedish Research Council DMP answers on **documentation**, **data description**, **data quality**, **storage**, **security**, and **who is responsible**.
5.  **Judge** what can be shared, what must stay protected, and how to use KI-supported AI tools (Copilot-first) responsibly — with disclosure and verification.

# What happens on each day

## Day 1 — Transparency and provenance

*Principle: research is only as trustworthy as the trail it leaves. Workflow that enacts it: structure and documentation.*

**Morning (self-study, 3 h)**

-   Orientation: why reproducibility matters, the 5-year test, the DMP assignment.
-   Read [Good Enough Practices](https://carpentries-lab.github.io/good-enough-practices/aio.html) **Part A** (Martin): Introduction; Data Management recommendations 1–6; Project Organization; Collaboration recommendation 1 (the README).
-   Read the [KI guidelines for research documentation and data management](https://staff.ki.se/research-support/research-data-management/plan-your-research-data-management/guidelines-for-research-documentation-and-data-management) (Johanna).
-   FAIR website with videos (Johanna).
-   Compare a good and a poor synthetic project folder — name the principle each one breaks (Johanna).

**Afternoon (TBL, 3 h)**

-   iRAT/tRAT on concepts (Martin): raw vs derived, provenance, FAIR vs open, ELN vs project folder.
-   Application 1: Draft manually or use Copilot to draft a folder tree for *your* project; if you use AI, keep the prompt and output; present to the team.
-   Application 2: folder + README for one shared global-health vignette, **stating the principle behind each choice**. Paste **data description** and **documentation** into the DMP. Inter-team critique against the 5-year rubric.
-   Exit ticket: one change to your own project, and why.

## Day 2 — Openness with boundaries, and accountability

*Principle: reproducible work is legible to others and honest about how it was made. Workflow that enacts it: tracked changes, disclosed AI use, a credible DMP.*

**Morning (self-study, 3 h)**

-   Read Good Enough Practices **Part B** (Martin): Keeping Track of Changes (all); Data Management recommendation 7; Collaboration recommendations 2–5.
-   KI guidelines on data sharing.
-   Metadata versus raw data.
-   Versioning so the project passes the 5-year test — a readable history of files and decisions (dated copies and a log, or Git).

**Afternoon (TBL, 3 h)**

-   iRAT/tRAT on versioning, collaboration, "as open as possible, as closed as necessary", AI disclosure.
-   Team application on students' **own** project packages: peer review against the 5-year rubric. Paste **data quality**, **storage**, **security**, and **who is responsible** into the DMP.
-   AI task: turn notes into a README and decision log, then verify and edit. Paste draft text into the DMP template.
-   Closing synthesis: principles revisited, what belongs in the data collection protocol, where to get KI support.

# Scope

**In scope:** the principles of reproducible and open research, and the workflows that enact them — folder structure, documentation, versioning, sharing boundaries, responsible AI use, and the six DMP areas in outcome 4.

**Out of scope** (point to other courses or course parts, do not teach here):

-   Programming, statistics, analysis pipelines, containers, and workflow managers.
-   Git beyond a short versioning option (K8F6106 covers this).
-   The **data collection protocol** — the assignment's second component. We only note where instruments and versions live.
-   Other SRC DMP questions (legal, ethics, accessibility, long-term storage, software, DOI, costs). Students finish those for the course assignment.
-   A separate lecture on metascience or the replication crisis. Principles are taught through the workflows.
-   More than one shared vignette, minute-level facilitator scripts, polished video, or new TBL hosting.
